intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

selected_hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, Praia da Marinha, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Walk the clifftop trail connecting nearby coves and take a refreshing swim in the sheltered bay. Snorkeling gear can be rented locally to explore the rich marine life beneath the surface.
experiences.location: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa, Central Algarve

experiences.name: Algarve Beachfront Wine Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Join a curated wine tasting session at a seaside quinta or beach club near Portimão, sampling regional Algarve wines including Vida Nova rosé, Marquês dos Vales whites, and local red blends. A sommelier guides you through the unique terroir of the region, pairing wines with local cheeses, presunto, and fresh seafood bites while enjoying ocean views.
experiences.location: Meia Praia Beach, Portimão, Western Algarve

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle by kayak from Praia de Benagil into the world-famous Algar de Benagil sea cave, a cathedral-like grotto with a natural skylight and a hidden beach inside. Guided tours depart from the beach and include stops at multiple sea arches and grottos along the coastline. A bucket-list Algarve experience best enjoyed in calm morning waters.
experiences.location: Praia de Benagil, Lagoa, Central Algarve

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset Cliffside Dining & Local Seafood
experiences.description: Dine at a rustic beachfront restaurant near Sagres Point, the southwestern tip of Europe, where you can feast on freshly grilled cataplana (seafood stew), percebes (barnacles), and grilled sea bass paired with a crisp local Alentejo white wine. Watch the dramatic Atlantic sunset over the cliffs of Cabo de São Vicente as the sky turns shades of orange and pink.
experiences.location: Sagres, Vila do Bispo, Western Algarve

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour & Barrier Island Beach Hop
experiences.description: Board a traditional wooden boat from Faro's waterfront and cruise through the Ria Formosa lagoon, a protected natural park teeming with flamingos, herons, and sea life. Stop at the pristine barrier island beaches of Ilha Deserta and Ilha do Farol, accessible only by boat, for a secluded beach experience far from the crowds. Includes a guided nature commentary.
experiences.location: Ria Formosa Natural Park, Faro, Eastern Algarve

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage and arrange transfer to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa (approx. 45–60 min by bus/taxi). Budget tip: Take the Eva Transportes bus from Faro to Lagoa/Carvoeiro area, then a short taxi to the boutique stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Lagoa Boutique Stay and freshen up. Take a gentle 10-minute walk down to Praia da Marinha to get your first look at the iconic golden limestone cliffs and turquoise waters. Explore the cliff-top coastal path for stunning views — completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearby village of Lagoa for a relaxed first dinner. Explore the small town square and get oriented with local shops and cafes.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastel de nata and coffee at the airport or on the bus — under €3
meals.lunch: Pick up a prego (steak roll) or bifana from a local snack bar near Lagoa town for €3–5
meals.dinner: Tasca do Zé in Lagoa — a no-frills local tasca offering grilled fish of the day (peixe do dia) with bread and salad for €10–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: September is an excellent time to visit Algarve — summer crowds thin out, temperatures remain warm (24–28°C), and prices drop. Keep receipts for budget tracking. Buy a reusable water bottle to save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Praia da Marinha at sunrise — one of Portugal's most photographed beaches. Arrive before 9:00 to beat any remaining tourists. Swim in the crystal-clear coves and explore the sea caves and rock arches along the shoreline. Entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the 'Seven Hanging Valleys Trail' (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos) — a spectacular 5.7 km cliff-top trail starting near Praia da Marinha toward Benagil. Enjoy dramatic coastal scenery, hidden grottos, and sea views. Completely free and one of the best walks in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa town for a relaxed evening. Visit the local mercado if open, or browse the small artisan shops. Enjoy a glass of local Algarve wine at a terrace bar.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay or a nearby pastelaria — coffee + toast with manteiga (butter) and doce (jam) for €2–3
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local Pingo Doce supermarket in Lagoa — bread, local cheese, cured meats, fruit, and water for under €6
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Barradas in Silves or a local grill in Lagoa — grilled sardines (sardinhas assadas) with potatoes and salad for €10–12

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys trail is moderate difficulty. Wear sturdy shoes, bring sunscreen and water. The trail ends near Praia de Vale Centianes — you can take a taxi back (€8–10) or retrace your steps.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — the historic Moorish capital of the Algarve, just 15 km from Lagoa. Take the local bus (Próximo/Eva line, ~€2 each way). Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€3 entry) with panoramic views over the town and orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves' charming old town on foot. Visit the Gothic Sé Catedral de Silves (free entry or small donation). Browse the riverside market stalls along the Rio Arade. Walk the ancient city walls and enjoy the peaceful, non-touristy atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa by bus. Enjoy a quiet evening at the boutique stay or a short walk around the local neighbourhood.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and croissant at a pastelaria in Lagoa before catching the bus — €2–3
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — a beloved local spot; try cataplana de peixe (fish stew) or grilled dourada for €11–15. Alternatively, grab a cheaper prato do dia (dish of the day) at a café for €7–9 including drink
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using supermarket ingredients at the boutique stay if kitchen facilities are available, or grab takeaway piri-piri chicken from a local churrascaria for €6–8

day_by_day.notes: Silves is one of the most underrated towns in the Algarve — far less touristy than Lagos or Albufeira. September is harvest season, so you may see orange and fig picking in the surrounding countryside. The bus journey takes about 25–30 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Benagil Cave (Algar de Benagil) — one of Portugal's most famous sea caves. Walk 2 km from Praia da Marinha along the cliff path to Praia de Benagil. Rent a kayak (€15–20/hour) or join a budget group boat tour (€15–20 per person) to enter the cave. Book in advance online for the cheapest rates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Praia de Benagil after the cave visit. Swim in the calm September waters. Walk back along the cliff path to Praia da Marinha, stopping at viewpoints along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Carvoeiro village (3 km from Lagoa) — a picturesque whitewashed fishing village with a small beach. Watch the sunset from the clifftop boardwalk at Algar Seco rock formations (free). Browse the village's small shops.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay or local café — galão (milky coffee) and tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese) for €3–4
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia de Benagil — fresh grilled fish sandwich or salad for €7–9
meals.dinner: O Castelo restaurant in Carvoeiro — budget-friendly menu with fresh seafood; try grilled lulas (squid) or arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) for €12–15

day_by_day.notes: Benagil Cave can only be entered by water — you cannot swim in from the beach safely. Budget kayak rentals are the most affordable option. Book boat tours early in the day or the evening before. September water temperature is around 21–22°C — perfect for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Visit Quinta dos Vales winery near Estombar (15 km from Lagoa — taxi or rideshare ~€12–15 one way). This is one of the Algarve's most accessible wineries offering guided tours and tastings. Book a standard tasting session (€10–15 per person) featuring local Algarve red, white, and rosé wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to explore the wine estate's sculpture garden and vineyard grounds (often included in the tour). Learn about the unique Algarve wine region, which uses grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco. Purchase a bottle of local wine as a souvenir (€6–10).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa. Visit the Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa — one of the oldest wine cooperatives in the Algarve, located right in Lagoa town. They offer informal tastings and sell local wines at very affordable prices (€1–3 per glass, bottles from €4).

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay — fresh fruit, yogurt, and local bread with coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery if offered (often a cheese and charcuterie board paired with wine for €8–12), or bring a picnic to enjoy among the vines
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Leão de Porches in Porches village — traditional Algarvian cuisine; try the açorda de marisco (seafood bread stew) or cabrito assado (roasted kid goat) for €12–16

day_by_day.notes: The Algarve wine region is often overlooked in favour of Alentejo or Douro, but produces excellent value wines. Quinta dos Vales requires advance booking — call or email ahead. The Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa (Rua de Lisboa) is walkable from most of Lagoa and is a fantastic budget wine stop.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Albandeira — a hidden gem beach just 3 km east of Praia da Marinha, accessible by a short cliff walk or car. Much quieter than Marinha, with a small arch and crystal-clear water. Spend the morning swimming and relaxing on the golden sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the coastline toward Armação de Pêra (8 km east). Visit the beach town and walk along the long sandy Praia de Armação de Pêra — one of the longest beaches in the Algarve. Explore the small 17th-century fortress chapel (free) at the western end of the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a beachfront bar in Armação de Pêra. Take the local bus back to Lagoa (€2). Alternatively, explore Lagoa's weekly market if it falls on this day.

meals.breakfast: Padaria (bakery) in Lagoa — fresh bread, butter, and local honey with coffee for €2–3
meals.lunch: Fish restaurant on the seafront in Armação de Pêra — carapau grelhado (grilled horse mackerel, a budget staple) with chips and salad for €8–10
meals.dinner: Cervejaria Marisqueira in Armação de Pêra or back in Lagoa — amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams in garlic and coriander) as a starter, grilled fish main, for €13–16 total

day_by_day.notes: Praia de Albandeira is reachable on foot from Praia da Marinha via the cliff path in about 30–40 minutes. Wear appropriate footwear. Armação de Pêra has good bus connections back to Lagoa via the EVA/Próximo network.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos — one of the Algarve's most beautiful historic towns, 30 km west of Lagoa. Take the train from Lagoa station to Lagos (€3.50 each way, about 35 minutes). Explore the stunning old town: visit the Igreja de Santo António (€3) and the adjacent Museu Municipal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ponta da Piedade — a spectacular headland with dramatic golden rock formations, sea arches, and grottoes just south of Lagos town centre (30-minute walk or short taxi). Enjoy the free viewpoints and cliff-top paths. Optionally take a short kayak tour of the grottoes (€20–25 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lagos' lively but charming historic centre. Browse the pedestrian streets and evening market stalls. Enjoy the sunset from the city walls before taking the train back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at Pastelaria Mira Rio in Lagos — €2.50
meals.lunch: Cervejaria Dois Irmãos in Lagos — a local favourite for budget seafood; prato do dia with wine for €8–11
meals.dinner: O Camilo restaurant near Ponta da Piedade (if budget allows, €15–18) or grab a bifana and local beer at a tasca in Lagos old town for €6–8 before catching the train back

day_by_day.notes: Lagos train station is a 10-minute walk from the old town centre. The train from Lagoa station runs regularly — check CP (Comboios de Portugal) timetables at cp.pt. Ponta da Piedade is most beautiful in the late afternoon light. Bring a jacket for the train journey home in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Slow morning — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and explore the immediate surroundings of Praia da Marinha on foot. Visit the smaller, less-visited coves accessible by the cliff path: Praia do Barranquinho and Praia de Vale Covo. These secret beaches are perfect for snorkelling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Second wine tasting experience: Visit Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's winery) near Guia/Albufeira (20 km east — taxi ~€20 or rideshare). They offer tours and tastings of their award-winning Vida Nova and Aneto wines. Budget tasting: €12–18 per person. Alternatively, visit the more affordable Quinta da Penina near Portimão.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa. Enjoy a quiet evening exploring Lagoa's town centre, visiting the Igreja Matriz de Lagoa (free), and having a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay — coffee, local bread, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach — supermarket provisions: local olives, presunto (cured ham), queijo (cheese), crusty bread, and Algarve wine for €7–9 total
meals.dinner: Restaurante Paraíso in Lagoa — a local favourite with excellent value; try the mixed grill or bacalhau à brás (shredded cod with egg and potato) for €10–13

day_by_day.notes: Adega do Cantor requires advance booking and is more of a boutique experience. For a truly budget option, the Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa remains the best value wine tasting in the area. September is harvest season — you may see grape picking at wineries, which is a special experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha. Take the bus from Lagoa to Portimão (20 min, ~€2). Explore Portimão's waterfront and the Museu de Portimão (€3 — an excellent museum in a converted fish canning factory). Visit the daily fish market along the riverside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Praia da Rocha (2 km south of Portimão) — a wide, dramatic beach with golden cliffs and a 16th-century fortress (Fortaleza de Santa Catarina, free entry). Swim and relax on the beach. Explore the fortress ruins and enjoy the views over the river mouth.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Portimão's lively evening atmosphere. The riverside area has many affordable restaurants and bars. Watch local fishermen return with their catch before heading back to Lagoa by bus.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and tosta at a café in Lagoa before the bus — €3
meals.lunch: Churrasqueira Valentim in Portimão — famous for grilled sardines and chicken; a full meal with wine for €9–12
meals.dinner: Tasca da Dona Barca near Portimão waterfront — traditional cataplana dishes and fresh fish for €11–15; or grab takeaway churrasqueira chicken to eat by the riverside for €6–8

day_by_day.notes: Portimão is one of the Algarve's largest cities and has a great authentic local atmosphere away from the resort areas. The Museu de Portimão is genuinely excellent and very affordable — highly recommended. Bus back to Lagoa runs until late evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Carvalho — a hidden beach near Carvoeiro accessible via a tunnel carved through the cliffs (free). Arrive early to have it almost to yourself in September. Swim in the sheltered cove and explore the rock pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Algar Seco rock formations near Carvoeiro on foot — a free coastal boardwalk through dramatic limestone formations, sea caves, and natural pools. Walk the full loop (about 1 hour). Visit the small chapel of Nossa Senhora da Encarnação in Carvoeiro village.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Praia de Carvoeiro — watch the sun set behind the white cliffs from the beach or the clifftop terrace bars. Have a drink at one of the village's terrace bars overlooking the beach.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay or local padaria — fresh bread and coffee for €2–3
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia de Carvalho or Carvoeiro village — prego sandwich and a beer for €6–8
meals.dinner: Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro — a long-standing local favourite; try the açorda de gambas (prawn bread stew) or grilled seabass for €12–15. Ask for the prato do dia for best value.

day_by_day.notes: Praia de Carvalho tunnel can be very crowded in summer but September is much quieter. The beach is not accessible for people with mobility difficulties. Carvoeiro is a 15-minute walk or short taxi from Lagoa boutique stay.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cape St. Vincent (Cabo de São Vicente) — the southwestern tip of continental Europe. Take the bus from Portimão to Sagres (change at Lagos if needed, total ~€8–10 return, 1.5–2 hours). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (€3) with its huge wind compass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local taxi or walk 6 km to Cabo de São Vicente — Europe's most southwesterly point. The lighthouse and cliffs are free to visit. The views are absolutely spectacular. Browse the artisan market stalls at the cape selling local crafts and honey.
day_by_day.evening: Return by bus to Lagoa (allow 2+ hours for the journey). This is a long day trip — enjoy a relaxed dinner back at base.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique stay before departure — coffee, juice, and toast
meals.lunch: Restaurant A Tasca in Sagres village — fresh grilled fish (the town is known for excellent seafood); prato do dia for €9–12
meals.dinner: Simple dinner back in Lagoa — a local tasca or takeaway; try a francesinha-style sandwich or piri-piri chicken for €7–10

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest day trip of the itinerary. Start early (aim to leave by 8:30) to make the most of the day. Cabo de São Vicente can be very windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The scenery is absolutely worth the journey. Check bus times carefully at rede-expressos.pt or eva-bus.com.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day at Praia da Marinha — your home beach for the trip. Spend a leisurely morning swimming, snorkelling among the rocks, and exploring the coves you may have missed. Rent a stand-up paddleboard if available (€15–20/hour) for a new perspective on the cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the local Lagoa market (Mercado Municipal de Lagoa) for fresh local produce, Algarve almonds, figs, carob products, and local honey. Stock up on affordable souvenirs: bottles of local wine (€4–8), medronho (arbutus berry spirit, €5–10), and almond sweets (doces de amêndoa, €3–5).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell wine tasting and dinner. Return to the Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa for a final tasting of Algarve wines. Then enjoy a special farewell dinner at the best local restaurant within budget.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed breakfast at the boutique stay — fresh local fruit, yogurt, coffee
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Marinha — fresh grilled fish or seafood salad for €8–10
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for the farewell dinner: Restaurante O Barradas in Silves or a top-rated local tasca — cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana, the Algarve's signature dish) shared between two for €25–30 total, including local wine

day_by_day.notes: The cataplana is the Algarve's most iconic dish — a copper pot stew of clams, prawns, fish, and vegetables. Sharing one between two people is both authentic and budget-friendly. This is the perfect way to end the culinary journey. Stock up on wine and local products at the cooperative — they ship internationally if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — check out of Lagoa Boutique Stay. Take one last walk to the cliff edge above Praia da Marinha for a final view of the stunning coastline. Pack any remaining local food and wine purchases carefully.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Faro Airport. Take the bus from Lagoa to Faro (change at Portimão or Albufeira, total ~€6–8, allow 1.5–2 hours). Arrive at the airport with plenty of time. Browse the airport shops for any last-minute Portuguese products: pastéis de Belém, Compal fruit juices, or local ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring the Algarve's beaches, cliffs, historic towns, and local wine culture.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão at a Lagoa café before departure — €2.50
meals.lunch: Airport café or grab provisions from a supermarket before heading to the airport — €5–8
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary for the trip: Accommodation (13 nights boutique stay), local buses/trains (~€50–70 total), beach activities and kayaking (~€60–80), wine tastings (~€40–60), food (eating local at tascas and snack bars, ~€20–30/day including all meals), entrance fees (~€20–30 total). Total estimated spend excluding accommodation and flights: €300–450 for 13 days — very achievable on a budget in the Algarve in September.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (~45 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle first walk down to Praia da Marinha, one of the most photographed beaches in the Algarve. Explore the golden limestone cliffs, sea arches, and crystal-clear turquoise coves. No swimming gear needed — just soak in the dramatic scenery and get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearby village of Carvoeiro for a relaxed first dinner overlooking the ocean. Browse the charming clifftop promenade and watch the sunset over the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport or in the car on arrival
meals.lunch: Light meal at a café near the hotel upon check-in — try 'Pastelaria Regional' style cafés in Lagoa for a bifana (pork sandwich) and fresh juice (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — a mid-range seafood restaurant with fresh grilled fish, local wine, and sea views (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally relaxed. Focus on arrival, orientation, and unwinding. September in the Algarve is warm (24–28°C), sunny, and less crowded than summer — ideal conditions throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Praia da Marinha properly — rent snorkeling gear locally and discover the incredible underwater rock formations, sea caves, and marine life. The water in September is warm (~22°C) and visibility is excellent. Arrive early (9:00–9:30) to beat day visitors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 15 minutes to the coastal boardwalk at Algar Seco, a spectacular series of rock formations and natural pools near Carvoeiro. Walk the clifftop trails and descend to the sea-level rock platforms. Visit the small bar built into the cliffs for a refreshing drink.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Lagoa town center (10 min drive) for a cultural evening. Visit the Igreja Matriz de Lagoa church, then settle into a tasca (traditional tavern) for dinner with local Algarvian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay or nearby café — fresh pastries, fruit, coffee (~€6–10)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the cliffs — pick up local bread, cheese, charcuterie, and fruit from a Lagoa supermarket or deli (~€10–15 for two)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Lagoa in Lagoa — traditional cataplana (seafood stew), local Algarve wine, and homemade desserts (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear water shoes for Algar Seco rock exploration. Snorkel rental is available in Carvoeiro village for approximately €10–15 per set.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting morning at Adega do Cantor (Guia, ~20 min drive) — the famous winery co-owned by Cliff Richard, producing award-winning Algarve wines including their signature Vida Nova rosé and red blends. Book a guided tour and tasting in advance (~€15–20 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Silves (~25 min from Lagoa) and explore the stunning red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves), the best-preserved Moorish castle in the Algarve. Walk the ancient walls for panoramic views over the orange groves and Arade River valley.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves old town — a charming medieval riverside town with excellent restaurants and a relaxed atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café Inglês in Silves or breakfast at the hotel — fresh orange juice (Algarve oranges are exceptional), toast, and eggs (~€8–12)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Silves after the castle — try Café Restaurante Marisqueira Rui for grilled sardines and local bread (~€15–20)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Ponte Romana in Silves — riverside terrace dining, excellent grilled fish and meat dishes, local wines (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Adega do Cantor tours should be pre-booked via their website. The Silves Castle entry is approximately €3–4 per person. September is harvest season in Algarve — vineyards are particularly beautiful.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Benagil — take a kayak or paddleboard tour from Carvoeiro beach (departs ~9:30 AM) to reach the famous Benagil Sea Cave, a cathedral-like cavern with a natural skylight opening. This is one of Portugal's most iconic natural wonders. Book in advance (~€25–35 per person for guided kayak tour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Praia de Benagil or neighboring Praia do Carvalho after the morning activity. These are smaller, more secluded coves accessible by short cliff walks. Bring a book and enjoy the September sunshine without the peak summer crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Carvoeiro village for a wine and tapas evening at one of the clifftop bars. Watch the golden hour light on the limestone cliffs.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the kayak tour — essential to eat well before paddling (~€8–12)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Benagil — grilled chicken piri-piri, fresh salad, cold beer (~€12–18)
meals.dinner: O Castelo or Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro — fresh catch of the day, local Vinho Verde, dessert of Dom Rodrigo (Algarve almond sweet) (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Benagil kayak tour is weather-dependent. Book with companies like Seafaris or Algarve SUP & Sea. Arrive at the meeting point 15 minutes early. Wear reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos (~35 min drive west). Begin with a walk through Lagos old town — explore the 16th-century city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the historic Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos), one of Europe's first slave markets, now a sobering and important museum (~€3 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos's stunning beach coastline — walk from Meia Praia to Praia Dona Ana and Praia do Camilo, connected by dramatic clifftop paths. Praia do Camilo, reached via wooden staircases through the cliffs, is a highlight. Swim in the sheltered turquoise coves.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagos town — a vibrant evening atmosphere with excellent restaurants and a lively but not overly touristy scene in September.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at a café in Lagos old town upon arrival (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — fresh seafood, local wines, outdoor terrace (~€20–28 per person)
meals.dinner: : A Forja Restaurant in Lagos — a beloved local institution serving traditional Portuguese meat and fish dishes in a rustic setting (~€22–32 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is very walkable. Park near the marina and explore on foot. The clifftop walk between beaches takes about 45–60 minutes and is one of the most scenic coastal walks in the Algarve.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Quinta dos Vales winery in Estômbar (~15 min from Lagoa) — a beautiful estate known for its sculpture garden, vineyards, and excellent wine production. Join a morning wine tour and tasting that includes a walk through the vines, winery visit, and tasting of 4–5 wines with local charcuterie (~€20–30 per person, book ahead).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Arade River estuary by taking a river cruise from Portimão (~20 min drive). These relaxed 2-hour boat trips wind through the natural wetlands, passing orange and almond groves, traditional fishing villages, and birdlife including flamingos and herons (~€25–35 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Portimão — a working fishing city with excellent, authentic seafood at lower prices than tourist-heavy coastal towns.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a café in Lagoa before heading to the winery (~€8–12)
meals.lunch: Wine and charcuterie tasting at Quinta dos Vales serves as a light lunch — supplement with local olives and bread purchased at the estate shop
meals.dinner: Tasca da Dona Amélia in Portimão — legendary local seafood restaurant, try the grilled dourada (sea bream) or amêijoas (clams) (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales also has a sculpture garden with over 70 large-scale artworks among the vines — allow extra time to explore. Portimão is also famous for its sardine grilling on the riverfront — if you see street grills, grab a portion (~€5).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge morning at Praia da Marinha. Pack a beach bag and spend a leisurely morning swimming, reading, and exploring the rock pools at low tide. This is your mid-trip relaxation day — no agenda.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the charming village of Alte (~40 min drive north into the Algarve hinterland) — one of the most picturesque traditional villages in the region. Explore the whitewashed houses, flower-draped streets, the 16th-century parish church, and the natural spring (Fonte Grande) where locals still gather. A world away from the coastal tourist trail.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast and enjoy a sundowner at a clifftop bar near Carvoeiro. Early, relaxed dinner and an early night.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel — treat yourself to the full spread (~€10–15)
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch in Alte at Restaurante Alte — hearty Algarvian mountain food: bean stew, roast pork, local bread, house wine (~€15–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Light dinner back in Carvoeiro — fresh salads, grilled fish, and local wine at a beachfront café (~€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Alte is a wonderful contrast to the coastal experience. The village is quieter on weekdays. Bring comfortable walking shoes for the cobblestone streets. The spring area has shaded picnic spots.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Sagres (~1 hour west) and visit Cabo de São Vicente — the most southwesterly point of continental Europe. Stand on the dramatic 75-meter cliffs at the edge of the known world. The lighthouse and fortress are open for visits. The wind and scale of the Atlantic here are unforgettable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres Fortress (Fortaleza de Sagres) — the massive promontory fortress associated with Henry the Navigator and Portugal's Age of Discovery. Walk the vast flat headland, see the mysterious wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos), and take in the wild Atlantic views. September is excellent for whale and dolphin spotting from the cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Sagres village — a small, end-of-the-world town with surprisingly good seafood restaurants and a relaxed surfer vibe.

meals.breakfast: Early start — grab coffee and a croissant in Carvoeiro before driving (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Vila Velha in Sagres — excellent fresh fish, locally caught, simple preparation, outstanding quality (~€20–28 per person)
meals.dinner: A Sagres or Restaurante Nortada in Sagres — fresh tuna steak (September is prime tuna season), local wine, ocean views (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is the windiest point in Portugal — bring a light jacket even in September. The drive along the Costa Vicentina (wild coast) north of Sagres is spectacular if you have time. Sagres Fortress entry is approximately €3 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to Ferragudo (~10 min from Lagoa) — a picturesque fishing village on the Arade River estuary, often overlooked by tourists. Walk the narrow cobblestone streets, visit the 16th-century Castelo de São João do Arade (exterior), and browse the small fishing harbor where boats still bring in the morning catch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting at Adega de Lagoa (Cooperativa Agrícola de Lagoa) — the historic wine cooperative in Lagoa town, producing wines under the Lagoa DOC designation since 1944. Taste their distinctive fig-based liqueur (medronho), local table wines, and fortified wines. Very affordable tasting experience (~€5–10 per person, walk-in friendly).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Praia de Carvoeiro — the small beach directly below Carvoeiro village, framed by cliffs. Enjoy the golden hour from the beach or the clifftop benches, then dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Ferragudo — fresh orange juice, toast with local honey and cheese (~€7–10)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Ferragudo at Restaurante Sueste — waterfront terrace, fresh grilled fish, exceptional views of Portimão across the river (~€22–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro — reliable mid-range restaurant with good cataplana and local wines (~€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is one of the most authentic fishing villages remaining in the Algarve — genuinely worth the short detour. The Adega de Lagoa is a functioning cooperative, not a tourist winery — a more authentic experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Faro (~1 hour east). Begin with the stunning Ria Formosa Natural Park — join a morning boat tour through the lagoon system, visiting barrier islands, salt pans, and wildlife habitats. September is ideal for birdwatching (flamingos, spoonbills, herons). Tours depart from Faro marina (~€25–35 per person, 2–3 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Faro old town (Cidade Velha) — enter through the Arco da Vila, visit the impressive Sé Cathedral (climb the tower for panoramic views, ~€3), and browse the archaeological museum inside the former convent. Faro is often skipped by tourists but has genuine historic character.
day_by_day.evening: Early dinner in Faro before the drive back, or return to Carvoeiro area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at a Faro café before the boat tour (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Restaurante 2 Irmãos in Faro — a Faro institution since 1925, excellent seafood rice and fresh fish (~€20–28 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dois Irmãos or return to Lagoa area — light dinner at a local restaurant (~€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ria Formosa boat tour in advance with companies like Formosamar or Lands. Faro Cathedral tower closes at 18:00 — plan accordingly. The drive back from Faro to Lagoa is easy on the A22.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final dedicated beach morning at Praia da Marinha — your home beach. Take a last long swim, explore any remaining rock formations, and appreciate what many consider the most beautiful beach in Portugal. Bring snorkeling gear for one last underwater session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the village of Monchique in the Serra de Monchique mountains (~50 min drive north) — a spa town surrounded by eucalyptus, cork oak, and medronho berry trees. Visit the ruins of the Franciscan convent, browse local craft shops, and taste medronho firewater at a local producer. The mountain scenery is a dramatic contrast to the coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast for a special dinner — this is your second-to-last night, so treat yourself to a slightly elevated dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast (~€10–15)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central de Monchique — famous for their espetada de lombo (pork skewer) and local sausages, hearty mountain food (~€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Leão in Carvoeiro or a waterfront restaurant — splurge slightly on a quality seafood dinner with a good bottle of Algarve wine (~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Monchique is known for its natural hot springs (Caldas de Monchique is a short drive below the main town). The road up to Fóia peak (902m, highest point in the Algarve) offers panoramic views from coast to coast on clear days.

day_by_day.morning: Final wine experience — visit Quinta da Penina or arrange a private tasting at a smaller local producer in the Lagoa DOC area. Alternatively, visit the Lagoa market (held on certain days) to buy local products: dried figs, almond sweets, local wine, and olive oil to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxed afternoon at a beach of your choice — revisit a favorite (Praia da Marinha, Praia do Carvalho, or Praia de Benagil) for a final swim. Pack a picnic and spend a slow afternoon appreciating the Algarve coastline one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — celebrate the end of the trip with a memorable meal. Choose the best restaurant you visited during the trip for a return visit, or try somewhere new.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy it fully on this penultimate day (~€10–15)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach — assembled from local deli and bakery: fresh bread, local cheese, presunto (cured ham), olives, fruit, and a bottle of Vida Nova rosé (~€20–25 for two)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo — your farewell dinner with waterfront views, exceptional fresh fish, and a toast to Portugal with a glass of local wine (~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to buy any remaining souvenirs and gifts. Local specialties worth bringing home: medronho firewater, Lagoa DOC wine, almond-based sweets (Dom Rodrigo, marzipan), and fleur de sel sea salt from the Ria Formosa.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — check out of the boutique stay. If your flight allows, take one last coffee at a café in Carvoeiro overlooking the sea. Pack the car and begin the transfer to Faro Airport (~45 min drive). Allow plenty of time for check-in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 days of beaches, wine, cliffs, history, and exceptional Portuguese food.
day_by_day.evening: Flight home.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão (milky espresso) at a Carvoeiro café — a perfect last taste of Portugal (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Light meal at Faro Airport or a café near the airport before departure
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Faro Airport (FAO) is small and efficient but can get busy. Arrive at least 2 hours before departure. Car rental return is straightforward. September flights are generally on time. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Faro Airport to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (approximately 45 minutes). Settle into your suite, unpack, and enjoy a welcome drink and amenities provided by the boutique property.
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, take a leisurely private guided walk down to Praia da Marinha beach — one of the most celebrated beaches in the Algarve. Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Enjoy a private beach setup arranged by the hotel with sun loungers, chilled towels, and sparkling wine.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel terrace overlooking the Atlantic. Dine at a premium local restaurant such as Ocean Restaurant (Vila Vita Parc, nearby Porches) — a two-Michelin-starred experience showcasing the finest Atlantic seafood and Portuguese haute cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (arrival day)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the boutique stay upon arrival — charcuterie, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and chilled Alentejo white wine
meals.dinner: Ocean Restaurant at Vila Vita Parc, Porches — tasting menu with wine pairing featuring premium Algarve and Alentejo wines

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in if possible given the 13:00 arrival. Pack light for the afternoon beach walk — the path to Praia da Marinha involves some steps carved into the cliffs.

day_by_day.morning: Indulge in a gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay featuring local pastries, fresh orange juice, artisan bread, regional cheeses, and smoked fish. Then embark on a private guided sea cave and grottos boat tour departing from Praia da Marinha or nearby Benagil. Explore the iconic Benagil Cave, hidden sea arches, and secluded coves only accessible by water — aboard a premium private vessel with chilled champagne on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a light lunch and a relaxing afternoon at the hotel's pool or private beach area. Optional: indulge in a signature spa treatment — a Portuguese-inspired body wrap using local cork, citrus, and sea salt — at the hotel spa or at nearby Vila Vita Parc spa.
day_by_day.evening: Drive or be chauffeured to Carvoeiro village for a sunset stroll along the clifftop boardwalk. Dine at Bon Bon Restaurant (Carvoeiro) — a Michelin-starred gem offering creative Portuguese cuisine with exceptional wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet spread at the boutique stay — local pastries, smoked swordfish, regional cheeses, fresh fruit platters, freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the hotel — grilled sea bass, garden salad, and a glass of Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Bon Bon Restaurant, Carvoeiro — Michelin-starred tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat tour and spa treatment at least 48 hours in advance. September sea conditions are typically calm and ideal for cave exploration. Carvoeiro is approximately 10 minutes by car from the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided wine tasting excursion to the Algarve's premier wine region around Lagoa. Visit Adega do Cantor (Sir Cliff Richard's celebrated winery) or Quinta dos Vales for an exclusive estate tour and barrel tasting. Learn about the unique Algarve terroir, indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco, and enjoy a guided tasting of premium reserve wines paired with local charcuterie.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine journey with a visit to a second premium estate — Quinta da Penina or Quinta da Franceza — for a comparative tasting experience. Enjoy a private vineyard picnic lunch curated by the estate chef, served among the vines with panoramic countryside views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a relaxing evening. Pre-dinner drinks at the hotel bar, then a private in-room or terrace dinner arranged by the boutique stay's chef — a curated five-course tasting menu featuring the day's wine discoveries paired with each course.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Private vineyard picnic — artisan bread, local olives, regional cheeses, cured meats, and estate wines
meals.dinner: Private chef's tasting dinner at the boutique stay terrace — five-course menu with Algarve wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange the private vineyard picnic with the estate at least 3 days in advance. Request a bilingual sommelier guide for the wine tour. Quinta dos Vales and Adega do Cantor both offer exclusive private tours for premium guests.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning yoga or meditation session on the hotel terrace or beach, arranged by the boutique stay's wellness team. After a leisurely breakfast, take a private guided hike along the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos) — one of Portugal's most breathtaking coastal walks, starting from Praia da Marinha and stretching toward Benagil and beyond. A private guide will share geological insights and local history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Praia de Albandeira or Praia do Carvalho for a private beach picnic lunch prepared by the hotel. Spend the afternoon swimming in secluded coves and exploring the natural rock formations. A private support vehicle carries your belongings and returns you to the hotel in comfort.
day_by_day.evening: Freshen up at the hotel and enjoy a pre-dinner cocktail at the bar. Dinner at Henrique Leis Restaurant (Almancil) — a legendary Michelin-starred restaurant offering avant-garde Portuguese-French cuisine in an intimate setting.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet hotel breakfast with freshly baked goods, local honey, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Private cliff-side picnic — lobster rolls, gazpacho, artisan cheeses, fresh fruit, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Henrique Leis Restaurant, Almancil — tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys Trail is approximately 6 km one way — wear comfortable walking shoes. September temperatures are warm (around 26°C) so bring sun protection and water. Henrique Leis requires reservations well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel followed by a private day trip to the historic town of Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Explore the magnificent red sandstone Silves Castle with a private historian guide, visit the Gothic Cathedral, and stroll through the charming old town streets lined with orange trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: After exploring Silves, visit a nearby artisan distillery or olive oil estate for a tasting experience. Quinta da Figueirinha near Silves offers premium olive oil and wine tastings in a beautiful rural setting. Enjoy a farm-to-table lunch on the estate terrace overlooking the Arade River valley.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel. Sunset drinks on the clifftop with panoramic Atlantic views. Dinner at Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo — a premium waterfront restaurant celebrated for its exceptional fresh fish and seafood, with views over the Arade River estuary.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table estate lunch at Quinta da Figueirinha — seasonal vegetables, grilled meats, estate olive oil, and local wines
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste, Ferragudo — fresh catch of the day, grilled whole fish, and premium Algarve wines

day_by_day.notes: Silves is approximately 25 minutes by car from the hotel. Arrange a private driver for the day. The Silves Medieval Fair typically occurs in August, but the castle is magnificent year-round. Book Restaurante Sueste in advance as it is very popular.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a slow, indulgent morning. Late breakfast on the hotel terrace. Full morning spa experience at Vila Vita Parc's award-winning spa (approximately 10 minutes away) — enjoy a couples' or solo luxury package including hydrotherapy, hot stone massage, and a traditional Portuguese facial using local botanicals.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the spa, head to Praia da Marinha for a private paddleboard or kayak session along the coastline, guided by a certified instructor. Explore sea caves and hidden beaches from the water at your own pace. Return to the hotel for a refreshing poolside lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private sunset catamaran cruise departing from Portimão or Lagos — sail along the Algarve's golden coastline, watch the sun dip below the Atlantic horizon with chilled champagne and canapés on deck. Return to port and transfer back to the hotel for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely late breakfast at the hotel — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, specialty teas and coffees
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the hotel — grilled octopus salad, fresh bread, and a glass of chilled Alentejo white wine
meals.dinner: In-hotel or nearby premium restaurant — Tasca da Marinha (if available locally) or a return to a favourite from earlier in the trip

day_by_day.notes: Book the Vila Vita Parc spa well in advance — it is one of the most sought-after wellness destinations in Portugal. The sunset catamaran cruise typically lasts 2–3 hours; confirm departure times based on sunset (approximately 19:45 in mid-September).

day_by_day.morning: Full day excursion to Lagos — one of the Algarve's most beautiful and historic towns. Depart after a leisurely breakfast with a private driver. Begin with a guided walking tour of Lagos old town: the historic slave market (Mercado de Escravos), the Igreja de Santo António with its stunning gilded baroque interior, the city walls, and the vibrant market square.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ponta da Piedade — a dramatic headland of golden limestone towers, arches, and sea caves just south of Lagos. Take a private boat trip through the grottos from the small pier below. Afterwards, enjoy lunch at a premium Lagos waterfront restaurant such as Casinha do Petisco or A Forja, known for their exceptional seafood and regional cuisine.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Lagos marina and browse artisan boutiques. Sunset drinks at a clifftop bar overlooking Meia Praia. Return to the hotel. Dinner at Restaurante Adega Vilalisa (Mexilhoeira Grande) — a rustic-luxury experience celebrating traditional Algarve cuisine with an exceptional wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Premium seafood lunch in Lagos — fresh oysters, clam cataplana, grilled tiger prawns, and regional white wine
meals.dinner: Adega Vilalisa, Mexilhoeira Grande — traditional cataplana dishes, slow-roasted meats, and an extensive Portuguese wine list

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is approximately 35 minutes by car from the hotel. A full private driver for the day is recommended. Ponta da Piedade boat trips are weather-dependent but September is typically excellent. Adega Vilalisa is a local institution — reservations essential.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided wine masterclass at the hotel or a nearby premium estate — a dedicated sommelier conducts an in-depth tasting session focusing on Portugal's most celebrated wine regions: Douro, Alentejo, Dão, and Algarve. Learn to identify varietals, understand terroir, and pair wines with food. Accompanied by a curated selection of premium Portuguese wines and artisan nibbles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxed afternoon at Praia da Marinha. Private beach setup with luxury sun loungers, a parasol, chilled towels, fresh fruit, and a dedicated beach attendant. Optional: snorkelling session in the crystal-clear waters around the rock formations guided by a local marine expert.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset photography session on the Marinha cliffs with a professional photographer — capture the extraordinary golden light over the Atlantic. Dinner at GUSTO by Heinz Beck at Conrad Algarve (Almancil) — a Michelin-starred restaurant by the acclaimed German chef, offering modern Mediterranean cuisine with exceptional Portuguese wines.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Gourmet beach picnic delivered by the hotel — lobster salad, chilled gazpacho, artisan bread, and a bottle of premium Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: GUSTO by Heinz Beck, Conrad Algarve — tasting menu with sommelier wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private sommelier masterclass through the hotel concierge. Book GUSTO well in advance — it is one of the most coveted reservations in the Algarve. The sunset photography session should be timed approximately 30–45 minutes before sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the dramatic Costa Vicentina — the wild, unspoiled Atlantic coast within the Southwest Alentejo and Vicentine Coast Natural Park. Depart after breakfast with a private driver. Visit Sagres and the legendary Fortaleza de Sagres — the clifftop fortress from which Portugal's Age of Discovery was launched. Explore Cape St. Vincent (Cabo de São Vicente), the southwesternmost point of continental Europe, with breathtaking ocean vistas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Sagres and its pristine beaches — Praia do Martinhal or Praia da Mareta. Enjoy a premium seafood lunch at Restaurante A Sagres or Pousada do Infante overlooking the dramatic coastline. Spend the early afternoon at the beach before heading back toward the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel. Relaxing evening with a private in-room couples' massage arranged by the concierge. Light dinner at a nearby premium local restaurant or an elegant in-room dining experience curated by the hotel chef.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet hotel breakfast before the day trip
meals.lunch: Premium seafood lunch in Sagres — fresh tuna tataki, grilled sea bream, local percebes (barnacles), and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Elegant in-room dining — chef's selection of cold seafood platter, regional cheeses, and a bottle of Alentejo red wine

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is approximately 1 hour 15 minutes from the hotel — a full day with a private driver is ideal. Cape St. Vincent can be windy even in September; bring a light layer. This is one of the most spectacular natural landmarks in Portugal and not to be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the hotel. Private cooking class with a local Algarve chef — learn to prepare traditional dishes such as cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana), amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams with garlic and coriander), and Dom Rodrigo (the Algarve's iconic almond and fig sweet). The class takes place in the hotel kitchen or a nearby culinary studio.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy the fruits of your culinary labour with a leisurely lunch. Afternoon at leisure — relax by the pool, read on the terrace, or take a gentle walk along the Marinha cliffs. Optional: visit the nearby Porches Pottery studio to select handcrafted Algarve azulejo tiles and ceramics as premium souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on the hotel terrace with a selection of local craft gins and tonics (the Algarve has a growing premium gin scene using carob, citrus, and herbs). Dinner at Restaurante Capote (Lagoa) — a sophisticated local favourite celebrating Algarvian cuisine with a modern twist and an impressive wine list.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during the morning cooking class — cataplana, clams, and traditional Algarve desserts, paired with estate wines
meals.dinner: Restaurante Capote, Lagoa — modern Algarve cuisine tasting menu with regional wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the cooking class through the hotel concierge at least 3 days in advance. Porches Pottery (Olaria Algarve) is a short drive from the hotel and offers beautifully crafted traditional blue-and-white ceramics — a quintessential Algarve souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided excursion to the Ria Formosa Natural Park — a stunning coastal lagoon system near Faro, one of Portugal's most important wetland ecosystems. Depart after breakfast with a private driver. Board a premium private boat for a guided tour of the lagoon's islands, birdwatching spots, and traditional fishing communities. Visit Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) for a walk on its pristine white sand beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lunch at Estamine restaurant on Ilha da Culatra or a premium waterfront restaurant in Faro — celebrated for its exceptionally fresh seafood sourced directly from the lagoon. Explore Faro's charming old town (Cidade Velha): the cathedral, Bishop's Palace, and Roman walls. Browse the boutiques and galleries of the pedestrian streets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel. Farewell pre-dinner drinks at the hotel bar with a curated selection of premium Portuguese digestifs — ginjinha, medronho (arbutus berry brandy), and aged port. Dinner at São Gabriel Restaurant (Almancil) — a Michelin-starred institution offering classic Portuguese fine dining with one of the finest wine cellars in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Waterfront seafood lunch in Faro or on Ilha da Culatra — fresh oysters, grilled razor clams, seafood rice, and chilled local white wine
meals.dinner: São Gabriel Restaurant, Almancil — classic fine dining tasting menu with exceptional wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Ria Formosa is approximately 45 minutes from the hotel. Arrange a private boat tour in advance. Ilha Deserta is accessible only by boat and is beautifully peaceful in September. São Gabriel is one of the Algarve's most prestigious restaurants — book well ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — begin with a champagne breakfast on the hotel terrace, celebrating the journey. Take one last private morning walk along the Marinha cliffs to savour the extraordinary landscape. Optional: a final sunrise or morning swim at Praia da Marinha — one of the world's most beautiful beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lagoa wine cooperative (Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa) — one of the oldest in Portugal — for a final premium wine tasting session and the opportunity to purchase bottles to take home. Spend the remainder of the afternoon at leisure: poolside relaxation, a final spa treatment, or a gentle drive through the Algarve's inland villages of Alte or Salir, known for their whitewashed houses, springs, and traditional character.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner — return to a favourite restaurant from the trip or book a special private chef's dinner at the boutique stay. A curated seven-course tasting menu celebrating the best of Algarve cuisine and Portuguese wines, served on the terrace under the stars with the sound of the Atlantic in the background.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on the hotel terrace — smoked salmon, eggs royale, fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, and Cava or Champagne
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa or a nearby premium café — local tapas, cured meats, and a glass of Lagoa reserve white wine
meals.dinner: Private farewell chef's dinner at the boutique stay — seven-course tasting menu with premium Portuguese wine pairing for each course

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private farewell dinner with the hotel at least 48 hours in advance. Purchase wines at the Lagoa cooperative to bring home — they can assist with packaging for travel. Savour every moment of this final evening on one of Europe's most spectacular coastlines.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final breakfast at the hotel. Pack and check out at leisure. Private luxury transfer arranged to Faro Airport. Stop en route if time permits at a local pastelaria for a final bica (espresso) and pastel de nata — a quintessential Portuguese farewell ritual.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry with you bottles of Algarve wine, artisan ceramics from Porches, local carob products, and memories of thirteen extraordinary days on Portugal's golden coast.
day_by_day.evening: In transit — homeward bound.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet hotel breakfast — a leisurely spread with all favourites from the trip
meals.lunch: Light snack at the airport or en route — pastéis de nata, local almond sweets, and a final bica
meals.dinner: In transit

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before departure for airport check-in and security. Faro Airport is approximately 45 minutes from Praia da Marinha.
